_note: Narrative pack for the NIS2 Quick Gap report. The generator does NOT free-write: boilerplate.* is inserted VERBATIM; executiveSummary.templates lines are composed by slot-substitution ONLY; consultantBlocks are seeded with data-derived facts plus a clearly-marked placeholder for the consultant to complete. Do not auto-assert legal conclusions.

structureOrder: path_forward_and_confidence (exec_path_forward composed incl. consultant_top_priorities + exec_confidence composed + not_determination verbatim)

templates.exec_verdict: This assessment finds that {clientName} has {verdictMaturityPhrase} against its obligations under NIS2, with significant gaps remaining in {weakestAreaName}. These gaps carry regulatory exposure, and the roadmap in this report addresses them.
templates.exec_verdict_nogaps: This assessment finds that {clientName} has {verdictMaturityPhrase} against its obligations under NIS2, with no applicable obligation assessed as Partially or Not Achieved.
templates.exec_scope: The assessment covered {applicableCount} applicable NIS2 obligations drawn from the cybersecurity risk-management measures (Article 21) and the governance (Article 20) and incident-reporting (Article 23) duties of Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
templates.exec_profile: Of these, {achievedCount} were assessed as Achieved, {partiallyCount} as Partially Achieved, and {notAchievedCount} as Not Achieved.
templates.exec_path_forward: The roadmap in this report sets out, in order of priority, the work to close the {gapTotal} obligations assessed as Partially or Not Achieved.
templates.exec_confidence: These findings rest on answers for {coveragePct} of applicable obligations ({confidenceLabel}). The conformance figure of {conformancePct} is given for context and is not a pass mark or a grade.
templates.exec_exposure_classification: {clientName} is classified as an {entityClassificationLabel} entity under NIS2.

verdictMaturityPhrases.substantial: substantial gaps in the measures required

gapConcentrationFragments.partialClause: foundations exist but are not yet fully in place
gapConcentrationFragments.absentClause: absent and need to be established

boilerplate.exec_partial_vs_absent: "Partially Achieved" means an obligation is recognised and some controls are in place but fall short of full conformance, so the remaining work is improvement and evidence. "Not Achieved" means the obligation is not yet met and the measures have to be established. Closing a Not Achieved gap usually takes more effort and cost, because there is nothing in place to build on.
boilerplate.regulatory_stakes: NIS2 obligations are legally binding, and for essential entities non-compliance has direct consequences. Members of the management body can be held responsible for the entity's compliance with the cybersecurity risk-management measures, and competent authorities can enforce compliance and impose financial penalties. After a significant incident, the reporting duties set fixed deadlines: an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month. Gaps in these areas are a regulatory exposure as well as a security weakness.
boilerplate.not_determination: This gap assessment is intended to support improvement and to prepare for engagement with the regulator. It is not a formal determination of NIS2 compliance, which only the relevant competent authority can make. The judgements are the consultant's, made against the obligations of the Directive.

consultantBlocks.consultant_exposure_seed: For {clientName}, the weakest area identified is {weakestAreaName}.{repExposureClause}
consultantBlocks.consultant_exposure_rep_clause: Incident-reporting obligations (REP) are currently assessed as Not Achieved, and these carry the statutory reporting deadlines noted above.
